a: at the point nearest the sea
t: A broken word in the Latin
p: The Latin has a word marked as corrupt here, so the base English fills the gap.

readings.en: assailed by sea the winter quarters of two cohorts, which was the nearest point to attack

why: The editor Fisher marks occupata with daggers, the sign that he judges the transmitted word corrupt. The base English reads "assailed by sea"; the free translation says only what the sure words allow, "at the point nearest the sea".
b: Fisher prints proximo †occupata† Oceano, with the word between daggers. Taken literally it would be "seized by the nearest Ocean," which does not fit the sentence. The Conversational English Translation keeps only the sure sense, near the sea, and adopts no emendation.

The base English ("He was then put in irons") has the same chain of subjects. Hordeonius is alive until he is murdered at 4:36, which also fits either reading.
